title: prototype-parity theme pass
acceptance: The shared theme declares fontFamilyMonospace with 'Space Mono' first (self-hosted via @fontsource/space-mono imported in apps/web), and every numeric metric cell in the leagues and athletes tables renders in the mono face at the same Mantine text size as neighbouring text cells, right-aligned
The theme radius scale is xs 0.125rem / sm 0.1875rem / md 0.3rem / lg 0.375rem / xl 0.5rem; person avatars remain circles and organisation avatars remain radius sm

Tooltip colors are set once in the shared theme so the surface follows the active color scheme in both light and dark modes (never inverts), with a test asserting the theme-level Tooltip defaults exist

Tables render verticalSpacing sm with toolbar rows py 4 and footer rows py xs, on both the leagues and athletes tables and their skeletons, which mirror the same paddings so no layout shift appears between states

The leagues header is one composed row - title with live count, inline search input, then the pill groups - with the search never detached in the page corner; the leagues columns are ordered # | League/Competition | Key Athletes | Nationalities | Athletes | IG Reach with numeric metrics at the right edge and widths redistributed per the design doc
docs/design/DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md numeric examples (container padding table, skeleton references) are updated to the shipped density values so the doc and code state the same tokens
pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, and pnpm build pass; all changed or new strings are translated in all 7 locales
notes: Executes PRD 'Amendment 2 - prototype-parity design pass (2026-08-19)'. Read docs/design/DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md 'Theme tokens (prototype parity)' first - it IS the spec, verified against the deployed prototype CSS. The theme package owns tooltip colors, radius, and the mono face; pages own layout and column order. @fontsource/space-mono is a new dependency in apps/web (same pattern as the existing @fontsource-variable/inter import in main.tsx); regular 400 + 700 weights suffice. Design-language skeleton rules still bind: bar heights stay CSS-var formulas so the density change cannot drift them; skeleton paddings must move together with the real toolbar/footer paddings. The athletes table adopts the same density tokens (state siblings across pages, not only within one page). Do not change any API contract - this phase is presentation only. Update the design doc's numeric examples in the same commit so doc and code agree (the doc's spacing tables currently state the old density).
